Specialty consult update: Using the available case stem only, the pattern strongly localizes to the neuromuscular junction and is most consistent with myasthenia gravis. Key features are fluctuating ocular symptoms (diplopia) plus fatigable proximal limb weakness affecting stair climbing and upper limbs, which argue against a primary myopathy or CNS lesion and fit MG best. Recommended next service line: neurology, ideally a neuromuscular specialist, for confirmatory testing and treatment initiation. Highest-yield next tests: AChR antibody panel and electrodiagnostics (repetitive nerve stimulation or single-fiber EMG); if respiratory/bulbar symptoms emerge, escalate urgently for possible myasthenic crisis evaluation.
